I will keep my full 12.0 mu in cotton this year. I have grown cotton for a long time, my land is not large, and there are only 2 people in my household, so I will stay with the crop I know best and manage it in a steady way instead of taking risks. Because I have well irrigation, I will rely on that to protect the crop if spring and early summer are dry. I will use improved seed rather than traditional seed because I want more even emergence and a more stable yield on limited land. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage because it is practical for my scale and lets me prepare the field quickly at the start of the season. I will apply a moderate-to-high fertilizer rate to support cotton growth, with nitrogen as the main nutrient and phosphorus and potassium added to keep the plants balanced. I will irrigate several times through the season, especially around establishment, flowering, and boll setting. I will also plan several pesticide sprays because cotton usually needs active pest control if I want to protect yield. My goal is not the highest possible output, but a stable crop I can manage with my experience, labor, and water access.
